audit_findings.title: The numerator and denominator represent different equity claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 non-controlling-interest net income was $35.628 million, 30.1% of the $118.2 million OE anchor; the 81.463 million denominator is 18.0% above the filed 69.015 million weighted-average diluted Class A shares
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE numerator starts with parent-attributable income but uses consolidated cash-flow adjustments, while the share denominator includes Class B/CC Units on an if-converted basis; this affects OE, per-share allocation, the historical trend and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, Cactus Inc. consolidates the financial results of Cactus Companies and its subsidiaries and reports a non-controlling interest related to the portion of CC Units not owned by Cactus Inc., which reduces net income attributable to holders of Cactus Inc.’s Class A common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim mismatch is demonstrated. Excluding the CC Unit Holders' earnings while including their equivalent shares tends to understate value, but consolidated depreciation, capital expenditure and working-capital adjustments can move the correction in either direction. The $35.628 million NCI income is large relative to the anchor, although the net OE correction remains unquantified without rebuilding the adjustments consistently.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild 2017-2025 OE either from consolidated earnings and cash flows divided by all Class A equivalents or from parent-attributable earnings and parent-attributable cash-flow adjustments divided by the corresponding Class A claim; then rerun the anchor, trend and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The TRA is a substantial omitted cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $267.048 million filed TRA liability at June 30, 2026, including $21.314 million current; $3.28 per valuation share and 11.5%-16.4% of stated scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: TRA payments consume cash available to Class A equity and must enter either projected OE as cash outflows or the equity bridge as a present-value deduction, but not both.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the total liability from the TRA was $ 262.9 million with $ 21.3 million reflected in current liabilities based on the expected timing of our next payment.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability and its absence from the stated bridge are demonstrated. Whether the valuation already captures it through OE is unresolved: the filing shows a $20.069 million TRA payment in 2025 operating cash flow, but the supplied methodology does not trace that payment or future payments into OE. If not captured there, the omission is material relative to every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Trace the 2025 TRA payment and forecast payments through the OE calculation, including the associated tax savings; deduct the appropriate present value or liability in the bridge only for amounts not already reflected in OE, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Baker Hughes holds a compulsory exit claim beginning in 2028
audit_findings.magnitude: $241.121 million redeemable non-controlling interest filed at June 30, 2026, equal to $2.96 per valuation share and 10.4%-14.8% of stated scenario equity value; acquisition-date net put/call fair value was $146.738 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The compulsory purchase obligation is a redeemable minority claim that reduces residual common equity unless its settlement and the minority's share of operating cash flows are explicitly modeled.
audit_findings.evidence: Generally beginning on January 1, 2028, the Baker Member has the right to sell to either the Joint Venture or the Cactus Member, and the Joint Venture or the Cactus Member, as applicable, shall be obligated to purchase all of the Membership Interests held by Baker Hughes Company (the “Put Right”).
audit_findings.explanation: This is no longer merely a possible future obligation. The June 2026 filing classifies it in mezzanine equity, treats redemption as probable and remeasures it to estimated redemption value. The stated bridge omits the $241.121 million claim, a scale capable of materially changing per-share values and the margin-of-safety threshold.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $241.121 million mezzanine balance to the put, call and 35% minority interest; incorporate the claim once in a current-perimeter valuation, using the contractual redemption calculation and consistent allocation of Cactus International cash flows, then rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The operating numerator and balance-sheet bridge use different business perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: Cactus International contributed $291.5 million of revenue and $0.5 million of net income in the six months ended June 30, 2026 and represented approximately 35% of consolidated revenue and 37% of consolidated assets; acquisition cash paid net of acquired cash was $301.011 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The DCF projects pre-acquisition OE while the bridge uses post-acquisition cash and liabilities; it consequently omits the acquired operations' earnings, reinvestment and working capital while not coherently allocating the 35% minority and acquisition claims.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 1, 2026, the Company acquired 65% of Baker Hughes Pressure Control LLC, which holds Baker Hughes Company's former surface pressure control business.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated and involves a business representing over one-third of current revenue and assets. Missing acquired earnings can understate value, while omitted minority, redemption and deferred-payment claims can overstate it. The target's first-half net income is depressed by purchase accounting and integration effects, so the net valuation impact cannot be inferred from $0.5 million alone.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild OE from post-close quarterly results or a reconciled current-perimeter run rate, separating purchase-accounting effects and transaction costs; include acquired working capital, maintenance capital, taxes, liabilities and the 35% minority claim, and rerun the bridge and scenarios on that same perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Deferred acquisition consideration is absent from the stated bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $24.5 million nominal deferred consideration, equal to $0.30 per valuation share and 1.1%-1.5% of stated scenario equity value; the June 2026 filing records $6.266 million fair value for the $10.0 million payment
audit_findings.mechanism: Any deferred purchase-price liability not included in projected OE or the redeemable-NCI balance should be deducted once from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the Baker Hughes Transaction, Cactus Companies is obligated to pay Baker Hughes Holdings $10.0 million on the first anniversary of the Closing Date and $14.5 million at such time as Baker Hughes Company ceases to be a member of the Joint Venture.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge does not separately capture the deferred consideration, although the filing records the present value of the $10.0 million payment and the treatment of the $14.5 million exit payment must still be reconciled. Even assuming the entire nominal $24.5 million were omitted, the maximum direct reduction is about $0.30 per share versus stated values of $19.93-$28.54 and a $70.16 market price, so it cannot change the valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Map the recorded $6.266 million and the $14.5 million exit payment to June 2026 liabilities and mezzanine equity, then deduct only the portion not already captured; document the adjustment without double-counting it with the Baker Hughes exit claim.

audit_findings.title: The anchor retains acquisition fees unlikely to recur indefinitely
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.059 million filed year-over-year increase in 2025 corporate expenses, equal to 10.2% of the $118.2 million anchor; exact transaction-fee portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing genuinely nonrecurring acquisition fees would increase normalized OE and proportionally raise operating value, while recurring integration and international overhead must remain in OE for their expected duration.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase was largely attributable to professional fees associated with the Baker Hughes transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The anchor's inclusion of the expense increase is demonstrated, but the filing says only that it was largely attributable to transaction fees and does not quantify the recurring versus nonrecurring split. As a scale test, adding the entire $12.059 million dollar-for-dollar to OE would raise scenario values by approximately $1.58-$2.45 per share, leaving the highest value near $30.99 versus the $70.16 market price. It can affect estimated value but not the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the invoice-level split of 2025 professional fees and the $7.1 million of transaction, reporting and accounting costs disclosed for first-half 2026; normalize only closing costs that will not recur and explicitly model the duration of integration and international-overhead costs.
